stem: The means of two samples of sizes 60 and 120 respectively are 35.4 and 30.9 and the standard deviations 4 and 5. Obtain the standard deviation of the sample of size 180 obtained by combining the two sample.

For a certain data, following information is available.

| | X | Y |
|---|---|---|
| Mean | 13 | 17 |
| S. D. | 3 | 2 |
| Size | 20 | 30 |

Obtain the combined standard deviation.
Calculate coefficient of variation of marks secured by a student in the exam, where the marks are: 85, 91, 96, 88, 98, 82
Find the coefficient of variation of a sample which has mean equal to 25 and standard deviation of 5.
A group of 65 students of class XI have their average height is 150.4 cm with coefficient of variance 2.5%. What is the standard deviation of their height?
_note: Printed as "coefficient of variance". The chapter defines only "Coefficient of Variation (C.V.)" (\(\text{C.V.} = 100 \times \frac{\sigma}{\bar{x}}\)); "coefficient of variance" is a nonstandard term and is almost certainly a misprint for coefficient of variation. Transcribed as printed. Also "have their average height is" is printed as shown (grammatical slip in the book).
solution: [Textbook misprint: the stem says 'coefficient of variance 2.5%' where the chapter defines only the Coefficient of Variation, and reads 'have their average height is 150.4 cm'. Solved as intended; the given \(n = 65\) is not needed for the answer.]
